summary: The note describes the Territory of Papua's administrative history. In 1949 the Territory of Papua and the Territory of New Guinea were joined in an administrative union called the Territory of Papua and New Guinea, which was renamed Papua New Guinea in 1971. Despite this union, Papua kept a distinct legal status and identity as a Possession of the Crown, while New Guinea was a League of Nations mandate and later a United Nations trust territory. This distinction lasted until the Independent State of Papua New Guinea was created in 1975.
one_line: Covers the Territory of Papua's 1949 administrative union with New Guinea and its distinct legal status until Papua New Guinea's independence in 1975.
key_facts: In 1949, the Territory of Papua and the Territory of New Guinea were established in an administrative union called the Territory of Papua and New Guinea.
The administrative union was renamed Papua New Guinea in 1971.
The Territory of Papua retained a distinct legal status and identity throughout its time in the administrative union.
The Territory of Papua was a Possession of the Crown.
The Territory of New Guinea was initially a League of Nations mandate territory.
The Territory of New Guinea was subsequently a United Nations trust territory.
The legal and political distinction between Papua and New Guinea remained until the advent of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea in 1975.
